facts.text: PKO Dziennik 13 Feb: 10Y SPW yield fell to 5% on 12 Feb; Jan CPI flash forecast 1.7% y/y (cons. 1.9%) vs 2.4% in Dec; no other CPI data before the 4 Mar MPC meeting, so the print could settle a March cut; Q4 GDP 4.0% y/y (1.0% q/q sa) close to PKO's 3.8% call.

Millennium daily 13 Feb (G. Maliszewski, C. Chrapek, A. Kaminski, A. Zalewski): Jan CPI forecast 1.9% y/y (lowest since Mar 2019) with elevated uncertainty from COICOP2018 and weights (Jan print may be revised in March); data should cement a March cut. But Q4 GDP 4.0% y/y above potential, faster wages and loose fiscal policy imply 'limited scale of possible cuts in this cycle'. Close 12 Feb: 2Y 3.44%, 5Y 4.26%, 10Y 4.99%; IRS 2Y 3.51, 5Y 3.70, 10Y 4.12.

Erste (Santander BP economists) Codziennik 13 Feb: 'significant strengthening of Polish bonds'; Q4 GDP 4.0% y/y in line with consensus. (Its recap of Kotecki's comments - March 25bp cut very likely, April possible, target 3.50-3.75% - was first published 12 Feb, pre-window.)

facts.text: PAP consensus for Jan CPI flash: 1.9% y/y, 0.6% m/m. PKO: a print below 1.9% could deepen the fall in yields; Millennium: stronger disinflation may extend the rally; EURPLN to stay 4.21-4.22.

GUS flash Jan CPI 2.2% y/y, +0.6% m/m (PAP consensus 1.9% y/y, 0.6% m/m; Dec 2.4% y/y). Food & non-alc. bev. 2.4% y/y (+1.3% m/m); alcohol & tobacco 7.0%; housing 2.9% (energy carriers 3.4% y/y, +1.9% m/m); transport -5.9% (fuels -7.1% y/y, -2.4% m/m). First print on COICOP 2018 but with 2025 weights; to be revised in March with the Feb data and new weights.

PAP close 13 Feb (T. Marek, PKO BP): weekly SPW yields -14-19bp, 10Y ~4.93% (multi-year low); CPI above consensus did not hurt bonds - market still sees a March cut as almost certain, MPC members signal high probability; demand helped by global flows and unsatisfied demand from the last MoF auction; expects the fall in yields to slow. EURPLN 4.20-4.23 range since Dec.
NBP: Dec 2025 current account -EUR 1,698m vs consensus -EUR 1,080m; exports +9.7% y/y (cons. +9.1%), imports +10.1% y/y (cons. +7.7%).

Credit Agricole MAKROmapa 16 Feb: forecasts Jan IP 3.0% y/y and construction -7.0% y/y (below consensus); strong demand for bonds last week; PL-DE 10Y spread at lowest since mid-2021; IRS curve lower on expected NBP easing; soft data slightly negative for PLN and IRS.

Erste/Santander Codziennik 16 Feb: Fitch's Poland analyst Milan Trajkovic told money.pl that if there are no grounds to reject the scenario of a GG deficit of 7% of GDP this year, 6.3-6.5% in 2027 and below 6% in 2028, Poland's rating may not be cut until 2027 or longer despite the negative outlook (Sept 2025); GDP growth beat Fitch's forecast in 2025 and may again in 2026. Erste: Jan CPI 2.2% vs its 1.7% forecast; core CPI estimated near Dec's 2.7%.

facts.text: PAP morning 16 Feb: PKO - consolidation of 10Y below 5%. Pekao - all key IRS nodes at new cycle lows; latest rally came with little ASW tightening (ASW still relatively high: ~60bp 5Y, ~85bp 10Y); sentiment 'very favourable', Wednesday auction should confirm; Jan wages key. Pekao: durable break of 4.20 EURPLN difficult.
GUS: 2025 goods trade deficit EUR 7.7bn; imports from China +13.3% y/y to EUR 57.9bn; Nov services output +6.2% y/y. Eurostat: Dec IP (wda) +6.9% y/y.

ING BSK: higher Jan CPI will not stop a March cut; recent MPC remarks suggest a 25bp March cut is 'essentially settled'; March NBP projection likely much better than November; rates may fall to 3.25% or even lower this year (vs 3.50% target seen by most MPC members). Reasons for the upside: food, energy carriers, and COICOP 2018 switch (+0.2-0.3pp to y/y).

Millennium (PAP 14:30): technical picture suggests potential for a slight upward correction of market rates; high demand can accompany elevated supply for a long time; Jan data mixed for rates (deeper IP slowdown, slower wage deceleration).

BPS weekly 16 Feb: Jan CPI 2.2% driven down by fuels; minimum wage +3.0% in 2026 (9.2% in 2025) to restrain inflation; MPC meets 3-4 Mar - if the projection confirms a durable return to target, majority may back a 25bp cut to 3.75%; data may strengthen market expectations of 50bp of cuts by end-2026. Regular Q4 GDP estimate due 2 Mar.
